title: Thread
description: A thread: one conversation with one harness, and the state that isn't its items.

Thread.description: A thread's own state. Sent whole in thread.updated and in snapshots.

id.description: The thread's id, chosen by the backend.

harness.description: The harness driver that runs it: "claude" or "codex" in v1.

model.description: The model the next turn uses, as the harness names it.

effort.description: Reasoning effort, as the harness names it (e.g. low, medium, high).

cwd.description: The working directory the harness runs in.

session_id.description: The harness's own session or thread id, used to resume it.

usage.description: Tokens used by the thread so far, over all its turns.

error.description: What went wrong, when status is error.

run.description: The harness process running the thread, if one is. Absent when it's idle with no process.

standing_answers.description: Answers that stand for the rest of the thread: a permission request for a tool one matches gets its outcome without asking. Added by a respond with always, and set by the app (when it creates the thread, or with set_options).

metadata.description: The app's own data, given when the thread was created. Backends store it and pass it to tools; they don't read it.

ThreadStatus.description: idle: no turn is running. running: a turn is running. waiting: a turn is waiting on a request (permission or question). error: the last turn failed, or the harness couldn't start; the next send tries again.

PermissionMode.description: default: ask (via the permission policy) for anything the harness would ask about. accept_edits: file edits in cwd are allowed without asking. plan: the agent plans and doesn't change anything. bypass: nothing is asked, and what would be is allowed. dont_ask: nothing is asked, and what would be (a question included) is denied.

StandingAnswer.description: An answer that stands for a tool: its kind, its MCP server (for an mcp tool) and its name, as in a PermissionRequest.

server.description: The MCP server, for a tool of kind mcp.

name.description: The tool's name, as in PermissionRequest.name.

Run.description: A harness process. A run started under the shim can outlive the backend: after a restart the backend re-attaches to it and sets reattached_at.

id.description: The run's id (with the shim, its run directory's name).

spawner.description: direct: a child process of the backend, which ends with it. shim: supervised by agent-threads-shim, so it survives a backend restart.

reattached_at.description: When a restarted backend last re-attached to the run. Absent if it never has.

cost_usd.description: What the tokens cost, when the harness says.
